culture_notes.note: "Bună ziua" (good day) is the safe greeting with strangers; "Salut"/"Hey" among young people. Use "dumneavoastră" (formal you) with older people; elderly men may still say "Sărut mâna" (I kiss your hand) to women as an old-fashioned courtesy. Thank you = "Mulțumesc" or the very common French loan "Mersi".
Bună dimineața (morning), Bună ziua (day), Bună seara (evening); Noapte bună only when parting at night. Pick by the scene clock.

Romanian is a Romance language; young educated people usually speak good English, older educated people often French/Italian/Spanish. Italians/Spanish tourists often half-understand Romanian signs. So bubbles: Romanian for locals with English translation; tourists speak their own language.

Foreign visitors to Bucharest searching online in 2024 came mostly from UK, US, Germany, Bulgaria, Italy, Greece, Israel, Netherlands and France; British searched for Therme, Americans for "Wednesday" filming locations and Romanian food, Bulgarians for Christmas markets/concerts. Use these origins for tourist personas.
Never assume a car will stop at a crosswalk; drivers can be inconsiderate. Locals joke and grumble about traffic, honking, sidewalk parking and buses; keep it good-humoured, never aggressive.

Typical words: mici/mititei (grilled minced-meat rolls), ciorbă de burtă (tripe soup), sarmale (cabbage rolls), papanași (doughnuts with sour cream and jam), covrigi (pretzels sold from street windows). Caru' cu Bere, Berăria H and Hanu' lui Manuc were the most-searched restaurants by foreign tourists in 2024.

Orthodox churches (Stavropoleos, Patriarchal/National Cathedral): people cross themselves when passing, speak quietly, women often cover their heads, shoulders/knees covered; avoid flash and ask before photographing services. Nuns/priests are greeted with "Bună ziua" or "Doamne-ajută" (God help); do not script jokes about clergy.
culture_notes.source: general Orthodox etiquette (no single source fetched from this environment - verify with church staff signage)

culture_notes.note: Romanians are hospitable and insist when offering something ("no" is often treated as politeness and the offer repeated) - vendors/elders can repeat an offer once before accepting a refusal. Respect for the elderly is valued; older men may kiss a lady's hand; handshakes are standard.

Vlad the Impaler is seen by many Romanians as a national hero; some are offended when he is equated with Count Dracula - so locals in bubbles push back ("Vlad Țepeș was one of ours, not a vampire!"). Opinions on Ceaușescu vary; some older people speak of him positively - an elder persona may be nostalgic, others critical; never caricature either.
Avoid lines implying Romanian is Slavic or that Romania was part of the USSR; never confuse Romanians with Roma people.
Unsolicited offers of help/taxis near tourist areas can be scams; locals recommend Bolt/Uber. A vendor/tout persona may push magnets or taxis politely; the player can just walk away.

Communism and Ceaușescu are top tourist interests ("Communism and communist buildings remain at the top of searches"). Locals talk about it with dark irony (e.g. calling the Memorial of Rebirth "the impaled potato"), but lines must stay factual and avoid mocking victims of 1989 (around 1,500 died).

Do not use ethnic jokes (in particular about Roma people) or Dracula/vampire clichés aimed at locals; Dracula appears only as souvenir-vendor patter and as a historical fact (Vlad III built the Old Princely Court).

1 March: mărțișor (red-and-white string trinkets) sold everywhere and given to women; December: "Crăciun fericit!" and the Christmas market in Piața Constituției; winter: "Ce ger!" (what frost); summer heatwaves: "caniculă" (summers often exceed 30 °C).

spots.name: Palace of the Parliament & Piața Constituției
spots.blurb: The heaviest building on Earth seen from the vast square at the head of Bulevardul Unirii.

footprint.note: ~440 m E-W x 410 m N-S. West edge cuts through the palace east wing so the whole 270 m main façade (east) stands inside the scene; the square, the head of Bulevardul Unirii with its first fountains, and the two curved 9-storey Ceaușescu-era blocks on Bd. Libertății frame it. Player is fenced out of the palace grounds except the public sidewalk; the visitor entrance (tours) is on the north side, Str. Izvor 2-4 / Bd. Națiunile Unite.

structures.name: Palatul Parlamentului (east/main façade)

dims.height_note: 84 m (en wiki) / 86 m above ground (ro wiki); 9 levels above ground + 9 underground (ro wiki), 92 m deep; OSM height=29 is the eave of the outer wings only

structures.style: Monumental socialist-realist neoclassicism (1984-1997), chief architect Anca Petrescu
structures.massing: Stepped ziggurat-like mass: wide 4-5 storey outer ring of wings, then set-back tiers climbing to a central cubic block crowned by a square attic/tower on the main E-W axis. East façade symmetric about the axis of Bulevardul Unirii; central projecting entrance pavilion (official entrance C4) with a tall colonnaded loggia/balcony (Sala A. I. Cuza opens onto it) above a ceremonial ramp and stair.

facade.material: light stone cladding over concrete (marble/travertine-like dressing, Romanian stone)
facade.windows: Very long regular rows of tall round-headed (arched) windows between paired pilasters/half-columns on every tier; dark bronze-tinted glazing (#3B3A36) in bronze/brown frames; ground storey rusticated with arcades
facade.ornament: Repeating colonnades and balustrades on each set-back terrace (white balusters), cornices with dentils, carved stone garlands, Romanian (Brâncovenesc) floral motifs in panels, three tall flagpoles on the forecourt facing the square (Romanian tricolour between two blue flags - EU and NATO, photo Bucharest Constitution Square.jpg); front garden: large flower parterre in red/gold, clipped hedges and conical thujas, a promenade and ground floodlights
facade.roof: Flat terraces behind balustrades; central tower block flat roof (panoramic terrace tour)

plaques.text: 270 m x 240 m, 84 m tall and 92 m deep underground: one of the largest administrative buildings in the world.
Built 1984-1997 by chief architect Anca Petrescu, who won the contest at 28, with a team of about 700 architects.
It weighs about 4.1 million tonnes, the heaviest building in the world, and sinks about 6 mm every year.
About 7 km² of old Bucharest were demolished and some 40,000 people relocated to make room for it.
Made almost entirely of Romanian materials: 1,000,000 m³ of marble, 3,500 t of crystal, 480 chandeliers.
In 1990 Rupert Murdoch offered US$1 billion for the building. The offer was refused.

interaction.title: Pace the Palace
interaction.desc: Walk/run the full 270 m east façade between two marker plaques; a timer and pedometer compare your time with how long it takes to walk the Pentagon's side and show "this is only one side". In December the square turns into the Christmas Market: buy a cup of vin fiert (mulled wine, shown as hot cocoa for kids) and ride the carousel.
interaction.true_to_place: The size is THE experience of the place; Christmas Market is really held here (2023-2025).

photo_angle.note: From the east edge of Piața Constituției by the "București 1459" clock, ~330 m from the façade, camera on the Unirii axis so the central pavilion is centred; at dusk the floodlights turn on. Postcard alt: from the Bd. Unirii median fountains (outside footprint).

seasonal_time_of_day: Summer: harsh midday sun from the south, heat shimmer over the setts; floodlights at ~21:00.
December: Christmas Market cabins fill the square (29 Nov-28 Dec 2025 edition), 30 m tree on axis, snow possible.
1 December (National Day): military parade, tribunes, crowd barriers.
Night: façade lit, square nearly empty.

plaques.text: Lipscani is named after Leipzig (Lipsca): traders here sold goods brought from the West.
Neighbouring streets keep the old guild names: Blănari (furriers), Șelari (saddlers).
Manuc's Inn was built in 1808 by the Armenian merchant Manuc Bei; talks for the 1812 Treaty of Bucharest were held here.
Curtea Veche: Vlad III (Dracula) dated a document from his "fortress of Bucharest" on 20 September 1459.
The Curtea Veche church (1559) is the oldest church in Bucharest kept in its original form.
Cărturești Carusel: an 1860 bank building, restored and reopened as a 6-floor bookshop in 2015. "Cărturești" is the chain's name, not "light".

interaction.title: Carousel climb & Dracula hunt
interaction.desc: Enter Cărturești Carusel and climb the white balconies to the top-floor bistro to unlock the atrium postcard; outside, find Vlad the Impaler's bust at Curtea Veche while vendors try to sell you "Dracula" magnets (say "Nu, mersi").
interaction.true_to_place: Carusel is the most photographed interior in Bucharest; Vlad III really founded the princely court.

Winter: terrace heaters, mulled wine, Christmas lights strung across lanes.
1 March: mărțișor stalls.
Mornings: delivery vans, cleaning trucks, almost empty.

spots.name: Stavropoleos, Caru' cu Bere & CEC Palace (south Calea Victoriei)
spots.name_ro: Stavropoleos, Caru' cu Bere și Palatul CEC
spots.blurb: A tiny 1724 Brâncovenesc jewel-church between a Gothic-Revival beer hall, a Beaux-Arts bank and the national history museum.

footprint.note: ~360 m E-W x 280 m N-S: Calea Victoriei from the Dâmbovița/Splaiul (S) to Str. Lipscani (N); Str. Stavropoleos and Str. Poștei pedestrian lanes to the east.

structures.name: Biserica Mănăstirii Stavropoleos (1724)

dims.note: OSM footprint; small single-nave church with a polygonal altar apse and a single tower/dome over the nave

facade.portico: open porch (pridvor) of slender carved stone columns (spiral/foliate shafts, carved capitals) carrying trefoil (three-lobed) arches, low stone parapet between columns
facade.walls: lower register: cream stone ashlar with blind trefoil arcades and a small barred window; middle frieze: band of round medallions with painted saints on a dark blue-grey ground framed by red-brown and ochre painted bands; carved stone cornice
facade.roof: terracotta clay-tile roof with a deep overhang on carved wooden brackets; octagonal cream drum (tower) with small rectangular windows under a red-tile conical/bell cap and an iron cross; separate red-tile domed roofs on the Ion Mincu courtyard building next door

structures.enclosure: low cream stone wall with square stone piers topped by urn finials and black wrought-iron grille panels (ring/quatrefoil pattern) around the church; black iron gate
structures.courtyard: Cloister-like courtyard (Ion Mincu building, early 20th c.) with arcades and a lapidarium of carved stone crosses and tombstones; flowers and climbing vines

structures.name: Caru' cu Bere (Str. Stavropoleos 5)
structures.history: Brewery opened 1879; restaurant opened 1899 in a Gothic-Revival building by architect Siegfried Kofczinski; historic monument B-II-m-B-19728; ~2,500 customers a day in 2014, 36% foreigners.

facade.details: pointed-arch windows with stone tracery, small corner turret, stained-glass, wrought-iron lanterns, carved wooden doors

structures.interior: 7 m high beer hall, Gothic columns, painted stucco vaults, carved oak staircases, Art Nouveau stained glass and murals

structures.name: Palatul CEC (Calea Victoriei 13)

dims.note: central glass-and-metal dome + four Renaissance corner domes

facade.details: entrance: semicircular arch on two pairs of composite columns; corner pavilions with pediments and coats of arms; central glazed dome with metal ribs

signage: CASA DE DEPUNERI, CONSEMNAȚIUNI ȘI ECONOMIE (inscription)

structures.name: Muzeul Național de Istorie a României (former Post Palace), Calea Victoriei 12

facade.details: portico of 10 Doric columns on a high base reached by 12 steps spanning the façade; allegorical sculpture

structures.extras: On the steps: bronze statue of Emperor Trajan (sculptor Vasile Gorduz, 2012) - naked emperor holding a Dacian wolf, much-discussed and photographed

ground.surface: small grey granite setts laid in overlapping fan/arc (segmental) pattern, framed by bands of large light granite slabs (photo: Biserica Stavropoleos B-II-m-A-19464)
asphalt, 2 lanes + bike lane, wide sidewalks of grey pavers
stone slabs and cobbles, grass strips

vegetation.summary: 108 OSM trees in footprint: notably 61 Prunus persica (ornamental) and Fagus, Tilia platyphyllos, Abies alba, Aesculus hippocastanum; courtyard of Stavropoleos has flowers, roses and climbing vines.

street_furniture: flagpoles on CEC and the museum (10 OSM flagpoles)
spots.lighting: CEC and history museum floodlit warm; Caru' cu Bere glowing interior and lanterns; church courtyard dim.
spots.backdrop: Calea Victoriei continues north towards Palatul Telefoanelor and Cercul Militar (eclectic 4-6 storey façades); Dâmbovița embankment and Splaiul Independenței traffic to the south; Old Town lanes (Lipscani spot) to the east; National Bank of Romania palace on Str. Lipscani to the north-east.

crowd.typical: Queue outside Caru' cu Bere at lunch/dinner, tourists photographing Stavropoleos portico, worshippers (lighting candles in the candle house), museum visitors posing with Trajan.

ambient_sounds: Byzantine chant from the church (choir founded 1994) on service times
restaurant bustle and folk music from Caru' cu Bere

plaques.text: Stavropoleos church was built in 1724 by the Greek monk Ioanikie Stratonikeas; the name means "City of the Cross".
Its choir sings neo-Byzantine chant, rare in Romania today, and the library holds Romania's largest Byzantine music collection.
Caru' cu Bere began as a brewery in 1879; the neo-Gothic beer hall opened in 1899.
The CEC Palace foundation stone was laid on 8 June 1897 in the presence of King Carol I; architect Paul Gottereau.
The History Museum, in the former Post Palace, holds a full plaster cast of Trajan's Column and the Romanian Crown Jewels.

interaction.title: Trajan's pose
interaction.desc: Strike the same pose as the bronze naked Trajan with the Dacian wolf on the museum steps for a photo challenge; then light a candle in the Stavropoleos candle house (quiet zone: running is slowed to walking in the courtyard).
interaction.true_to_place: The Trajan statue is the most joked-about statue in the city; candle-lighting is what locals actually do here.

photo_angle.note: From Str. Stavropoleos at the north-west corner of the church looking south-east at the west porch with its carved stone columns and painted upper walls (OSM: long axis E-W, altar to the east); alt: CEC Palace from the Calea Victoriei crossing at [44.43160,26.09690] heading 320.

seasonal_time_of_day: Easter night: candle processions in the courtyard.
Summer: queue at Caru' cu Bere, outdoor tables.
Winter: snow on the church eaves, warm light from the beer hall.

spots.name: Romanian Athenaeum & Piața Revoluției
spots.blurb: The domed 1888 concert hall in its garden, and the square where the 1989 Revolution toppled Ceaușescu.

footprint.note: ~400 m E-W x 470 m N-S along Calea Victoriei from Biserica Kretzulescu (S) to Str. Episcopiei/George Enescu (N); includes Grădina Ateneului, the Royal Palace (National Museum of Art) façade, Central University Library, the former Central Committee building (Ministry of Internal Affairs) with its balcony, and the Memorial of Rebirth.

structures.name: Ateneul Român
structures.style: Neoclassical with eclectic/romantic touches; architect Albert Galleron (France), built 1886-1888, extended to 1897
structures.massing: Circular drum crowned by a large ribbed dome (total 41 m) behind a temple front: Ionic peristyle of 8 columns (6 front + 2 side) on a high podium with a broad flight of steps; two small lateral corner towers/pavilions

facade.dome_note: dark grey-green metal-clad dome with radial ribs and a small lantern; names of Romanian scholars incised around the dome base (Miron Costin, Gheorghe Șincai, Dimitrie Cantemir, Ion Heliade Rădulescu, Timotei Cipariu)
facade.mosaics: five round mosaic medallions of rulers under the peristyle (Neagoe Basarab, Alexandru cel Bun, Carol I, Vasile Lupu, Matei Basarab) on gold ground
facade.inscription: ATHENEUL ROMAN (sic, old spelling with H) carved on the frieze under the pediment
facade.pediment: triangular pediment with dentil cornice and acroteria (palmettes; winged figures at the corners)
facade.columns: 6 fluted Ionic columns across the front + 1 behind each end, on a stylobate reached by ~10 broad steps
facade.doors: three tall carved oak double doors with glazed iron-grille upper panels
facade.side_windows: tall narrow windows with ornate wrought-iron grilles in the side wings; square windows with star/lattice grilles in the attic of the wings
facade.drum: drum ringed with circular medallions (lyres) between pilasters; names of scholars carved on the frieze below the dome

structures.name: Grădina Ateneului
structures.note: small formal garden in front: lawns, flower beds, gravel paths, benches; bronze statue of Mihai Eminescu (Gheorghe D. Anghel, 1963) on a tall pedestal

crowd.typical: Concert-goers in evening wear before 19:00 concerts (George Enescu Festival every odd year in September), guided "Calea Victoriei - Piața Revoluției" tours (most popular Visit Bucharest tour 2024), students at the library, protesters occasionally.

plaques.text: The Athenaeum was partly funded by public subscription: "Dați un leu pentru Ateneu!" (Give one leu for the Athenaeum!).
Inside, a 75 x 3 m fresco by Costin Petrescu circles the concert hall, telling Romanian history from Trajan to 1918.
On 29 December 1919 the Athenaeum hosted the vote ratifying the union of Bessarabia, Transylvania and Bukovina with Romania.
On 21 December 1989 Ceaușescu's speech from the Central Committee balcony here turned into the revolt that ended his regime.
The Memorial of Rebirth (2005) is a 25 m marble pillar; locals nicknamed it "the impaled potato".
The Carol I statue recreates Ivan Meštrović's 1930 equestrian statue destroyed by the communists in 1948; unveiled in 2010.

interaction.title: Give one leu for the Ateneu
interaction.desc: Drop a virtual 1-leu coin in the donation box by the steps (homage to the 1880s fundraising slogan) to open the doors and peek at the fresco and the concert hall; on the square, stand on the spot below the CC balcony and hear an archival-style crowd ambience.
interaction.true_to_place: The leu campaign is the Athenaeum's founding story.

photo_angle.note: From the south-east corner of Grădina Ateneului near the Eminescu statue looking north-west at the portico and dome (OSM: Athenaeum centroid 44.441321,26.097215).

seasonal_time_of_day: September of odd years: George Enescu Festival crowds and banners.
21-22 December: commemorations, candles at the memorial.
Spring: blossoming trees in the garden.
Night: illuminated dome is a classic postcard.

spots.name: Arcul de Triumf
spots.blurb: Bucharest's 27 m triumphal arch for the First World War and the 1918 union, in a busy roundabout on Kiseleff.

footprint.note: ~300 m x 300 m centred on the roundabout of Piața Arcul de Triumf (Șos. Kiseleff / Bd. Prezan / Bd. Averescu / Bd. Al. Constantinescu). Walkable: the central island around the arch (reached via signalised crossings), sidewalks and the entrance of King Michael I Park to the north-east. Traffic circulates as ambient (walk-only scene).

structures.name: Arcul de Triumf

dims.note: single vaulted opening; passage aligned with Șos. Kiseleff (NNW-SSE); internal stairs in the piers lead to a roof terrace

structures.style: Classical, modelled on the Paris Arc de Triomphe; architect Petre Antonescu; skeleton 1922 (temporary stucco reliefs), definitive 1935-1936 in Deva granite with Rușchița marble sculpture; restored from 2014

facade.details: attic with long carved inscriptions on all four sides; medallions "Bărbăția" (Ion Jalea) and "Credința" (Constantin Baraschi) on the north face; bronze medallions of King Ferdinand and Queen Maria on the south face; royal coat of arms reliefs under the vault; WWI battle names inside the vault

plaques.text: The arch is 27 m high on a 25 x 11.5 m base; the opening is 11 m high and 9.5 m wide.
First built in 1922 for the coronation of Ferdinand and Maria with plaster reliefs; rebuilt in granite in 1935-1936.
Designed by Petre Antonescu; sculptors included Ion Jalea, Constantin Baraschi, Mac Constantinescu and Dimitrie Paciurea.
The communists removed the King's and Queen's effigies; bronze medallions of Ferdinand and Maria were put back after 1989.
Earlier temporary arches stood in Bucharest in 1848, 1859, 1878, 1906 and 1918.

interaction.title: Read the arch
interaction.desc: Walk around the four faces: each inscription you stand in front of is read aloud/shown translated; collecting all four plus the 12 battle names in the vault unlocks the terrace (open Apr-Oct Tu-Fr 10-18, Sa-Su 11-19; Nov-Mar Tu-Su 9-17 per OSM) for a view down Kiseleff. On 1 December the parade passes through.
interaction.true_to_place: The inscriptions are the arch's story; the roof terrace is really open to visitors.

Autumn: golden linden/plane leaves on Kiseleff.
Night: floodlit arch with light trails of cars (long-exposure photo opportunity).

plaques.text: Opened on 10 May 1936 by sociologist Dimitrie Gusti in the presence of King Carol II; the 4th open-air museum in Europe.
Over 100,000 m² with 123 authentic peasant households, 363 monuments and over 50,000 objects from all regions of Romania.
The first buildings were dismantled in their villages and brought to Bucharest in 56 railway wagons.
The wooden church from Dragomirești (Maramureș), built 1718-1722, is the museum's centrepiece and logo.
A fire on 20 February 2002 destroyed 19 structures, including houses from Voitinel, Straja and Fundu Moldovei.
In 2017 the museum had about 800,000 visitors, 68% of them foreigners.

interaction.title: Draw water from the well
interaction.desc: Use a well sweep (cumpănă) to lift a bucket, then walk the alley to the Dragomirești church and strike the toaca (wooden semantron) rhythm on feast days; collect a stamp from 5 regional households (Maramureș, Transylvania, Oltenia, Muntenia, Moldova) for the "village passport".
interaction.true_to_place: Wells with sweeps, toaca and region-grouped households are exactly what the museum shows.

photo_angle.note: From the lawn ~40 m south-west of the wooden church (OSM way/277782593 at 44.47145,26.07900) looking NE up at the west tower spire with the graveyard crosses in the foreground.

seasonal_time_of_day: Spring (Easter): painted-egg fairs.
Summer: festivals, folk dances, long evenings.
Autumn: Târgul Meșterilor Populari craft fairs, falling leaves on shingle roofs.
Winter: snow on steep roofs - most photogenic; Christmas carol (colinde) events.

plaques.text: The park covers about 187 ha, of which 74 ha is Lake Herăstrău.
The marshes were drained in 1930-1935 and the park opened in 1936 as the National Park.
It was named Carol II Park, then I. V. Stalin Park (with a Stalin statue), Herăstrău in 1956 and King Michael I Park in 2017.
"Herăstrău" comes from "ferăstrău" (saw): water-powered sawmills once stood on the Colentina river.
Mammoth bones and Neanderthal-era flint tools were found in the Herăstrău sand quarry.

spots.name: Spring Palace (Ceaușescu Mansion)
spots.blurb: The private home of Nicolae and Elena Ceaușescu for 24 years: gold-plated taps, a mosaic swimming pool and peacocks in the garden.

footprint.note: ~280 x 280 m in the villa district of Primăverii: Bd. Primăverii 50 with the mansion, its walled garden (original plot 14,830 m²) and the quiet embassy-lined boulevards around it (Lithuanian and South Korean embassies, UN House). Interior is ticketed (guided tours).

structures.name: Palatul Primăverii (Bd. Primăverii 50)
structures.osm: way/549676146 (likely main building, 53.5 x 42.3 m, by size; annex way/549676153 32 x 30.7 m probably the pool wing; museum grounds way/38236017) - verify against refs
structures.history: Built 1964-1965 (architect usually credited: Aron Grimberg-Solari; some sources say Cezar Lăzărescu), home of the Ceaușescu family 1965-1989; opened to the public in March 2016.

facade.style: Neoclassical-revival villa (1960s build in historicist style): cream/white stucco walls, ground floor with large round-arched windows in arched recesses (wooden frames + ornamental iron grilles), modillion cornice, first-floor terrace with white turned balusters, deep eaves with coffered soffits, low hipped roof with red clay tiles (photo 20180411 135853, CC0)

boundary.desc: street boundary on Bd. Primăverii: ~0.9 m grey granite-clad plinth wall with ~1.3 m black wrought-iron fence (scroll and fleur-de-lis panels), tall pines/cedars and deciduous trees behind

structures.interior: Gold-leaf bathroom (gilded taps), indoor swimming pool hall with a vast 1960s mosaic (green/blue tesserae), winter garden, cinema room, Elena's dressing rooms, Murano chandeliers, carved wood ceilings, carpets

structures.name: Garden
structures.note: Lawns, rose beds, a small pond/fountain, mature trees and the resident peacocks (11 reported) - descendants of Ceaușescu's birds

structures.name: Bulevardul Primăverii
structures.note: Quiet tree-lined boulevard with villas of the former communist nomenklatura, embassies behind high fences, guard booths, cafés (Utopia Coffee Bar) - house of Ion Iliescu is on a neighbouring lot (OSM way/549676148)

vegetation.summary: Mature lindens, plane trees, pines and spruces in villa gardens; clipped hedges and fences with ivy along the boulevard; rose beds in the palace garden.

street_furniture: high fences and guard booths at embassies
spots.lighting: Residential street lamps; palace interior chandeliers glow in winter dusk.
spots.backdrop: Low 2-4 storey 1930s-1960s villas, 7-storey residential blocks on Str. Cehov to the west.

crowd.typical: Small guided groups (Romanian or English tours), communism-tour buses; quiet neighbourhood with diplomats, drivers, dog-walkers. Ceaușescu House was the most-searched museum by foreign tourists in 2022 and 2024 (Visit Bucharest).

ambient_sounds: quiet: birds, peacock calls from the garden, footsteps on gravel, occasional car

spots.blurb: Bucharest's oldest public garden (1847-1854): rowing boats on a winding lake, chess players and the Writers' Rotunda.

footprint.note: ~440 m x 410 m covering the central lake (410 x 140 m, 19,500 m²), the Rotonda Scriitorilor, the chess tables ("La Șahiști"), the French Heroes monument and the main entrances on Bd. Regina Elisabeta (N) and Bd. Schitu Măgureanu (W). Park total ~16 ha, English landscape style.

plaques.text: Cișmigiu is the oldest public garden in Bucharest, laid out from 1847 by Wilhelm Mayer, former director of the Imperial Gardens in Vienna; opened in 1854.
The name comes from "cișmegiu", the official who looked after the city's public fountains (Turkish çeşme = fountain).
In the winter of 1883 the frozen lake hosted ice-skating competitions; skating is still a winter tradition here.
The Writers' Rotunda (1943) gathers the busts of 12 great Romanian writers, from Eminescu to Creangă.
Swans and pelicans were brought to the lake after the park was enlarged in the 1880s.

interaction.title: Row or skate
interaction.desc: Summer: rent a rowing boat at the Debarcader and row around the island; winter: skate on the rink. Any season: watch a game at "La Șahiști" - the old men comment on your moves if you try one.
interaction.true_to_place: Boats, the winter rink and the chess players are Cișmigiu's defining rituals.

spots.name: People's Salvation Cathedral (National Cathedral)
spots.blurb: The tallest and largest Orthodox church in the world (127 m), with a gilded dome rising behind the Palace of the Parliament.

footprint.note: ~400 m x 420 m on Dealul Arsenalului: the cathedral (121 x 71 m footprint), its 11,600 m² piazza, the underground-chapel entrances and Calea 13 Septembrie with its 9-11 storey 1980s blocks to the south as backdrop; the Palace of the Parliament south façade bounds the north-east view.

structures.name: Catedrala Națională
structures.style: Romanian revival synthesis: Renaissance-revival high dome on a drum with a 16-arch peristyle, Romanesque façade towers, Neo-Byzantine bell tower; six octagonal towers around the dome; bell tower (campanile) at the west end

facade.material: light stone cladding (cream/white) over brick masonry
facade.dome: cupolas clad in Tecu Gold brass (gilded copper look), ribbed with embossed medallion panels and a decorated gold band at the base; tower drums white with arched windows between engaged colonnettes (photo June 2023)
facade.cross: 7 m / 7 t gilded cross installed 8 April 2025
facade.doors: 27 double-leaf 5.5 m-high bronze-plated doors with 61 saint bas-reliefs
facade.window: Ascension stained-glass window 5.5 x 15 m above the main entrance
facade.mosaics_exterior: mosaic icons in lunettes over portals

structures.bells: 6 bells totalling 32.2 t; the largest 25.19 t at 60 m in the bell tower, heard 15-20 km away

vegetation.summary: 174 OSM trees: rows of Tilia cordata (81) and Aesculus hippocastanum (78) along Calea 13 Septembrie and the slopes; Fraxinus americana, Quercus robur, Rhus typhina.

street_furniture: candle-lighting stands (lumânărar) in a separate pavilion
bus stop "Palatul Parlamentului" (route 136) on Calea 13 Septembrie
spots.lighting: Dome and towers floodlit golden at night, visible across the city.
spots.backdrop: North: Palace of the Parliament south façade (Calea 13 Septembrie entrance); south: 9-11 storey 1980s apartment blocks (Bl. 53-91) with ground-floor shops (Mega Image, Help Net pharmacy).

crowd.typical: Pilgrims and worshippers, especially on Sundays, feast days (Ascension = Heroes' Day, St Andrew 30 Nov) and since the 2025 consecration; tourists coming from the Palace; priests and nuns; candle and icon stalls.

ambient_sounds: bells (deep 25 t bell) at service times
Byzantine chant from loudspeakers on feast days

plaques.text: At 127 m (133 m to the top of the cross) it is the tallest and largest Orthodox church building in the world.
It holds the world's largest collection of church mosaics, about 25,000 m², made with Venetian Murano glass.
The main bell weighs 25.19 t, was cast in Innsbruck in 2016 and can be heard 15-20 km away.
The altar was consecrated on 25 November 2018; the mosaics on 26 October 2025, when the cathedral opened permanently.
The 11,600 m² piazza can hold over 23,000 people; the whole 11-hectare complex 125,000.

interaction.title: Light a candle & ring time
interaction.desc: Light a candle at the candle pavilion (for the living on one side, the departed on the other - a real Orthodox custom), then stand on the piazza at noon to hear the great bell. Quiet zone: no running on the piazza steps during services.
interaction.true_to_place: Candle-lighting and the record bell are what visitors do and talk about.

photo_angle.note: From the south-west corner of the piazza (OSM pedestrian area relation/16698908, 13,270 m² wrapping the church) looking ENE at the west front: bell tower (86 m) over the main portal with the Ascension stained-glass window, gilded central dome behind. Calea 13 Septembrie runs ~130 m south; Parcul Catedralei (under construction) lies north towards the Palace.

seasonal_time_of_day: 30 November (St Andrew) and Ascension: huge pilgrim crowds.
Easter night: candle-lit Resurrection service on the piazza.
Night: gilded dome glowing.
Summer: heat on the open stone piazza.
